subject: Discovery recap: timeboxing demo cadence and next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alexis Chen <alexis.chen@aeronimbus.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronimbus.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: timeboxing demo cadence and next steps

Alexis / Samir — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery (short):
- Primary use case: low-latency inference for real-time telemetry enrichment in AeroNimbus control plane.
- Key constraints: strict SLA on 95th percentile latency, data residency concerns for EU customers, expected peak concurrency ~150 rps.
- Stakeholders: Alexis (Platform), Samir (Security), and prospective pilot team in Berlin.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Technical deep dive + pilot design (60–75m): go over sample payloads, model selection, and latency SLOs.
2) Security quick-check (30m): Samir to confirm any additional evidence needed for pilot (SOC2 scoping, audit logs).
3) Scheduling: propose a 4-week pilot with rotating demo windows so we can include US, EU, and APAC contributors without repeatedly inconveniencing the same folks.

Proposed cadence (first pass): I put together a lightweight rotation we can pilot for 4 weeks (attached playbook + sheet). Each week we run one 75-minute deep-dive at a different timeband so AeroNimbus' cross-region team can attend at least once in the cycle.

Attachments: redwood-timebox-rotation-playbook.pdf, redwood-timebox-rotation-sheet.xlsx

Please reply with the best 2–3 slots that work for your team next week and any constraints (e.g., Samir: prefers no pre-noon PT meetings). If this looks good, we can lock the first pilot session and send calendar invites.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alexis Chen <alexis.chen@aeronimbus.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronimbus.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: timeboxing demo cadence and next steps

Thanks Mina — this was a helpful recap. A couple quick notes from our side: 

- We like the rotating approach in principle; avoids always asking the same EMEA/APAC engineers to do late/early calls.
- Availability constraints: Berlin pilot folks are generally available 14:00–17:00 CEST. US SREs can do 08:00–11:00 PT but prefer not earlier than 08:00. APAC (SG) attendees can join 09:00–11:00 SGT but not overnight.
- Security: Samir, can you confirm whether a short pre-read (SOC2 summary + network diagram) is ok as evidence for the initial pilot?

Proposed two candidate windows next week that would work for at least one representative from each region (we can rotate full-team coverage):
1) Tue 30 Jun 2026 — 08:30 PT / 11:30 ET / 16:30 BST — likely OK for US morning + EMEA afternoon
2) Wed 1 Jul 2026 — 23:00 PT / 02:00 ET / 07:00 SGT — only if we rotate APAC-friendly weeks (this is late for US, early for APAC)

We prefer option 1 for initial pilot. If Redwood can run the first session on Tue 30 Jun 08:30 PT, we'll aim to bring technical leads from Berlin and a subset of platform SREs.

—Alexis
Alexis Chen
Head of Platform | AeroNimbus
alexis.chen@aeronimbus.com | +44 20 7946 0998

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alexis Chen <alexis.chen@aeronimbus.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronimbus.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: timeboxing demo cadence and next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Alexis — option 1 sounds ideal to get broad coverage without burning the same people. Below is a compact pilot proposal and the rotation scheme we recommend for transparency (we'll keep it lightweight):

Pilot proposal (4 weeks):
- Week 1 (Tue 30 Jun): US-morning / EMEA-afternoon deep-dive — 08:30 PT (75m) — cover architecture walkthrough + sample payloads.
- Week 2 (Tue 7 Jul): EMEA-morning / APAC-evening deep-dive — 14:00 BST / 22:00 SGT — rotate so APAC can catch the session the following week.
- Week 3 (Tue 14 Jul): APAC-morning / US-evening deep-dive — 09:30 SGT / 18:30 PT — this favors APAC attendance.
- Week 4 (Tue 21 Jul): Consolidation session — overlap slot to gather pilot feedback and next steps.

Timeboxing rules (short):
- Each session is 75 minutes: 30m demo & architecture; 30m pilot design + data/SLAs; 15m Q&A & action items.
- Rotate the heavy-lifting (presenter/recording owner) across Redwood and AeroNimbus to distribute on-call/coverage load.
- We'll publish an agenda and attach a short pilot checklist before each session.

I attached a one-page playbook and an availability sheet (redwood-timebox-rotation-sheet.xlsx) that auto-generates a rotating calendar for the proposed dates.

Action items:
- Alexis/Samir: confirm Tue 30 Jun 08:30 PT for the first session (I'll send the invite once you confirm).
- Marcus/Laura: can you confirm who will own week 1 and week 3 presentations from Redwood? Prefer one of you cover week 1 (US slot) and rotate week 3 to alternate.
- Samir: quick yes/no on the SOC2 pre-read as acceptable initial evidence.

If everyone agrees, I'll lock the series and share calendar invites + agenda doc.

Thanks —
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

I'll also attach the simple runbook snippet into the invite (presenter checklist + recording notes).

—Marcus
